vectors.title: eddsa-jcs-2022-expires-hour-24: must be invalid
vectors.clarify: The proof's expires is a W3C Data Integrity dateTimeStamp, which is an XML Schema 1.1 dateTime: its lexical form admits endOfDayFrag (24:00:00), so 2999-01-01T24:00:00Z is lexically valid there; the fixture note 'hours run 00-23' is the RFC 3339 range that SPEC.md applies to issuedAt and expiresAt, not to proof members. A task-force decision is needed on which range governs proof timestamps. Not gating.

vectors.title: eddsa-jcs-2022-created-hour-24: must be invalid
vectors.clarify: The proof's created is a W3C Data Integrity dateTimeStamp, which is an XML Schema 1.1 dateTime: its lexical form admits endOfDayFrag (24:00:00), so 2026-09-15T24:00:00Z is lexically valid there; the fixture treats hour 24 as malformed under the RFC 3339 range that SPEC.md applies to issuedAt and expiresAt, not to proof members. A task-force decision is needed on which range governs proof timestamps. Not gating.

vectors.title: eddsa-jcs-2022-small-order-key: must be invalid
vectors.clarify: RFC 8032 section 5.1.7 step 3 checks [8][S]B = [8]R + [8][k]A' and says it is 'sufficient, but not required, to instead check [S]B = R + [k]A''; neither decoding (section 5.1.3) nor verification requires rejecting a public key of small order, and this signature satisfies both equations. Refusing it is the stricter verify_strict practice, which neither SPEC.md nor the Data Integrity EdDSA text requires. A task-force decision is needed on whether the baseline requires strict verification. Not gating.

vectors.title: eddsa-jcs-2022-mixed-order-r: must be invalid
vectors.clarify: RFC 8032 section 5.1.7 step 3 lets a verifier check either the cofactored equation [8][S]B = [8]R + [8][k]A' or, 'sufficient, but not required', the cofactorless one, and section 8.8 notes the choice changes which signatures are valid. This fixture satisfies only the cofactored equation, so a verifier that follows the RFC's primary equation accepts it. Neither SPEC.md nor the Data Integrity EdDSA text requires the cofactorless check. A task-force decision is needed on whether the baseline fixes one equation. Not gating.
